title: sum_amounts_for_subject wired into total_computation, replacing the inline scan it duplicated
goal: DRY up total_computation's own inline amount-scanning loop (found to be functionally identical to lab.common.rules.sum_amounts_for_subject, just reimplemented by hand) into one shared, directly-callable function.
method: brain.reason's own total_computation output checked against a direct call to sum_amounts_for_subject on the identical passages, with and without a mixed-in rule-shaped passage, confirming they agree and that the rule-exclusion default matches brain.py's existing, already-measured behavior.
results_prose: brain.reason's total_computation stage over two fact passages ($100 + $50): 'total 150 [P1, P2].'. With a threshold-rule passage mixed in (its own $500/$25 must NOT be counted as line items): 'total 150 [P1, P2].' -- still 150, the rule's own numbers correctly excluded. Calling sum_amounts_for_subject directly on the same passages gives the identical total/sources brain.py's stage produced (150.0, ['P1', 'P2']), confirming one real implementation, not two independently-written scans that happen to agree today. skip_rule_passages=False recovers the OLD (pre-2026-11-10-fix, lab.tests.support-era) behavior of counting everything, 675.0 -- available for a caller who genuinely wants that, but never brain.py's own default.
conclusion: lab.common.rules.sum_amounts_for_subject -- moved to lab.tests.support as test-only, moved back once this DRY gap was found -- is now the one implementation of the cross-passage amount scan total_computation needs, with the rule-passage exclusion brain.py's stage already required folded in via skip_rule_passages=True (the default). brain.py no longer carries its own copy of this scan.
scale_down: Two fact passages, one rule passage -- a proof the shared function reproduces brain.py's exact prior behavior, not a new capability measurement (calc.sum_amounts's own arithmetic was already proven in EXP-007/014).
models_used: None -- regex span extraction and arithmetic, both deterministic, unchanged by this refactor.
